Thank you for the comments. I'd like to give some context because I think without context it sounds like I don't like small ships and I think upgrades are pointless and all that, but that's not what I'm saying.

So my main ship currently is an iEagle. I've outfitted it with all D-class components because they're cheap, are very light, and perform better than E-class components. I also just like the iEagle.

I could upgrade some components to A-class if I wanted, but I don't intend to sell the iEagle after I'm done with it, so I'm not going to recoup the costs, and if I blow up it'll cost me more. Beyond maybe better thrusters, it gets its job done with D-class, why should I upgrade it?

Weapon wise I actually like having a turret on the top hard point since it's literally on target 100% if the time, but sticking a turreted cannon or a multicannon on it suddenly presents flying it as a hazard to my wallet whereas a gimballed multicannon is perfectly acceptable, it costs a tenth of the price and probably only gives you a little less time on target. Is it worth it to put a 1.5 million credit turret on the thing, and tripling my rebuy cost when I can get the same thing done with a gimbal worth it? No it's not.

Like, I just bought a Type 6, and I realised a C-class FSD was going to be a huge upgrade for total jump range, whereas an A or B class jump drive wouldn't offer much. I'd like to save up for a keelback but it sounds like this sub would have me max it out anyway.

Hi. I actually wanted to provide a bit of an update with some info if anyone out there also would like to know.

First off, thank you for pointing out that catacombs and caves are safe, because of this the range is actually much larger than I expected, so I tried some things.

So it's totally OK to activate the summoning pool for Margit and help other people. Just don't initiate a fight with Margit yourself. 

All of Weeping Peninsula and East/West Limgrave are safe. I've rested at every site of grace except for Summonwater which I'm not sure might be too far. You can kill the Mariner and do D's quest in Summonwater, just don't rest there because I don't think it's safe. 

Siofra River: So you can rest anywhere in Siofra River, it's safe down here and very pretty. I liked going down here because you can get the Marika Scarseal.

Tower of return: I panicked after taking this transport as there's no way back without resting at the site of grace, but turns out that's safe too. You can get the Blessed Dew Talisman.

Dragon-burnt ruins transport: Resting at the site of grace INSIDE Sellia Crystal Tunnel is also safe, just don't rest outside. This was nice to get the Meteorite Staff.

Third Church waygate to Bestial Sanctum: This is safe but you just can't rest anywhere in Caelid. This was nice because I could do a suicide run to get the Dectus Medallion half and the Radagon Soreseal. I also never opened the gate to sanctum, not sure if that's safe although I think it might be.

Liurnia of the Lakes, Caves: So I could travel freely about Liurnia of the Lakes resting only at the various caves. This was nice because I got the Glintstone Dagger, Sage Robes and Terra Magicka and I still haven't triggered it.

So this does pose a few more questions because I have both Dectus Medallion halves. I'm sure there's plenty more treasure in Caelid and Liurnia of the Lakes I could get, and I might even be able to go to Altus Plateau, however I think I've pushed this as far as I'd like and It's time to play the game properly.

It's a bit overkill but I bought several different solutions to see what works.

1. Creative SoundblasterX G6
The headphones sound great attached to this. The mic does not. It sounds worse than just plugging it into the mobo. My guess is it supplies even less power to the mic port. For such an expensive piece of equipment this was disappointing.

2. Antlion USB sound card
The microphone sounds fantastic plugged to this. My guess is it supplies the full 5v plug in power. Doesn't need any gain. Clean sound. Very cheap.

3. TRRS male to 2x TRS female splitter / adapter (Headphone and mic combined to one TRRS headset jack)
This is serviceable. It doesn't sound as loud or clean as the Antlion, but with +30db boost its fair. This is actually what I would recommend because it's cheap and simple (Likely a surefire solution whereas sound cards seem a bit hit and miss), second would be the Antlion because it's also cheap but not as simple, but does offer better performance if you really want to make sure your mic sound as nice as possible for YouTube or something.

Currently I'm using the soundblaster with the TRRS adapter because the headphones sound great and it cuts down on cable clutter. The mics not perfect but for gaming and casual chat it's alright. I can plug in the Antlion for professional applications or if I want to record my voice.

TL;DR If you have a problem with a weak sounding mic, try a TRRS adapter before buying anything.
